transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-19
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen, Luis Ortega, Hannah Park, Jonas Kim (Redwood) / Ben Holloway, Priya Nair, Samantha Lee, Marco Ruiz (Aureus)

Summary:
Quick tactical sync to align co-sell responsibilities, validate pilot success criteria, and triage network/security gating for a private deployment pilot. Primary blockers: network egress rules, SSO/SAML mapping, and partner margin split clarity.

Topics:
- Pilot scope and acceptance metrics
- Dedicated vs hosted routing for early pilot
- Security docs & compliance checklist
- Commercial split and referral margin mechanics
- Next-gen handoff to Aureus infra for scale test

[00:00] Maya Chen: ok hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll do a tight agenda, uh two main buckets commercial and technical, and then next steps. Ben? are you on from Aureus?
[00:32] Ben Holloway: yep, Ben here, thanks Maya. Quick high level we want to validate latency and cost for real-time shipment tracking, and confirm we can keep data in our VPC for PII rules.
[01:05] Priya Nair: and just to add, procurement wants a clear pilot SOW and estimated TCO so Samantha can run the vendor checklist.
[01:28] Samantha Lee: yeah procurement's timeline is fast, we need price ranges not just ballpark.
[01:45] Maya Chen: understood. Luis from SE side will walk infra constraints and then we'll cover pricing splits. Luis?
[02:10] Luis Ortega: thanks, hi everyone. Quick note, we recommend starting with Redwood Dedicated for the pilot — predictable throughput for the short test — but we can also show a hosted fallback in case capacity spikes. Dedicated avoids egress surprises if you want VPC peering.
[02:45] Marco Ruiz: when you say "VPC peering" — is that the private deployment or you mean dedicated within redwood's cloud? we need to make sure traffic doesn't route through public endpoints.
[03:12] Luis Ortega: good call — we have two flavors: Redwood Dedicated is reserved capacity in our infra (tenant isolated) which can be placed in a cloud region and peered to your VPC; Redwood Private is customer-managed private control plane (on-prem or VPC) for full isolation. For the pilot we can do Dedicated with VPC peering to reduce ramp complexity.
[03:46] Ben Holloway: if we do dedicated peering, what's the expected round-trip add for tokens? we've got 200ms SLOs for tracking updates.
[04:12] Luis Ortega: in our benchmarks, peered dedicated typically adds 10-25ms overhead vs host co-located, but that depends on your region and path. we'll provide test numbers. I'll attach perf samples in the doc.
[04:40] Priya Nair: security — we need SOC2 attestation and also want to see how KMS integrates, we use AWS KMS with external key policies.
[05:02] Hannah Park: we have a SOC2 report and a KMS integration guide. For Redwood Private we can support BYOK flows; for Dedicated we integrate with customer KMS over an approved connection. We'll share the security pack link.
[05:28] Samantha Lee: procurement asked about retention and audit logs — can you show what the logs surface look like?
[05:48] Maya Chen: yes, the Console exposes token-level cost breakdown and trace hooks. Hannah will share the screenshots.
[06:12] Jonas Kim: quick ops note — during the pilot you'll want a KV cache warming plan, since shipment history has heavy prefix locality; caching reduces token cost significantly. Luis will share cache configs.
[06:40] Marco Ruiz: we also use strict egress filters; will your dedicated nodes need specific outbound IP allowlist?
[07:01] Luis Ortega: yes we give a small set of egress IP ranges for dedicated pools; for peered VPC those are less relevant but our control-plane endpoints may need allowlist. We'll provide the CIDR blocks.
[07:30] Ben Holloway: circling back to pricing — Maya, you mentioned co-sell split. How do we expect margins to sit for resale vs referral?
[07:50] Maya Chen: good question. We're proposing a referral rebate for Aureus on net-new bookings introduced by your sales team, and a reseller margin if you resell Redwood Dedicated as part of a packaged solution. The exact percent depends on committed volume — Luis will run some scenarios in the sheet.
[08:18] Luis Ortega: I'll put a few tiers: pilot->proof->scale, and show net margin impact if you commit to a 12-month reserved capacity.
[08:40] Priya Nair: procurement will not accept open-ended commitments without SLA credits. What SLAs can Redwood offer for Dedicated?
[09:02] Maya Chen: our Dedicated contracts include uptime SLOs and latency targets we can put in the SLA; we also have automatic fallback routing policies to hosted for brief outages. We'll include terms in the draft SOW.
[09:28] Samantha Lee: ok that helps. Regarding the pilot timeline — we prefer a 2-week functional pilot then a scale week. Can you map milestones?
[09:46] Hannah Park: yes from onboarding to live pilot: Day 0-3 infra setup & peering, Day 4-10 run tests / validation, Day 11-14 initial customer traffic, Week 3 scale to steady-state. We'll document runbook items.
[10:12] Maya Chen: let's talk risk: biggest technical risks are SSO mapping for user-scoped requests and the egress constraints Marco called out; commercial risk is clarity on who owns the end-customer contract if Aureus packages Redwood as part of their offering.
[10:45] Ben Holloway: on SSO, we use SAML and have SCIM for user provisioning. Will Redwood surface token-level authorization per user?
[11:02] Luis Ortega: we support token scoping and can map SAML attributes to RBAC. For pilot we'll recommend a per-service account model then move to attribute-based mapping during scale. Some of the SCIM fields may need normalization — sometimes our auto mapping drops underscores — little things in transcription: sorry, I mean mapping quirks we've seen.
[11:34] Priya Nair: noted — we can supply a sample SAML assertion.
[11:45] Maya Chen: competitor note — Ben, you mentioned CumulusAI in earlier thread; have you run any perf or price comparisons?
[11:58] Ben Holloway: we ran a quick bench — Cumulus offered lower list price but lacked VPC-peering and the ops tooling that Redwood showed. OpenEndpoint gave on-prem but with a much longer ramp. So this co-sell plus Redwood's console is attractive.
[12:26] Luis Ortega: also, caching and batching levers are big cost differentiators — we can model cost with and without prefix caching to show savings.
[12:50] Maya Chen: sounds good. Let's get into the pilot acceptance criteria — Priya, what do you need?
[13:04] Priya Nair: must hit 95% of updates <200ms p95 for shipment lookups, tokens cost per event under $0.003 in pilot shape, and end-to-end encryption in transit with KMS keys.
[13:26] Jonas Kim: we'll capture p95 numbers and token accounting in the pilot spreadsheet.
[13:40] Marco Ruiz: on telemetry — we need structured traces to map requests back to shipments. Do you support a correlation ID passthrough?
[13:55] Luis Ortega: yes, Console supports trace hooks; we recommend injecting a correlation id and we can correlate tokens with that trace.
[14:12] Maya Chen: ok commercial detail — if Aureus resells and bundles Redwood, what does handoff look like? who owns support?
[14:32] Hannah Park: we normally do joint-support for the first 90 days then transition to the reseller (Aureus) with a runbook. We'll also include an escalation path to Redwood for infra incidents.
[14:55] Samantha Lee: good — procurement wants that in the SOW.
[15:10] Ben Holloway: can we get a sample SOW and pricing by early next week?
[15:22] Maya Chen: yes. I'll send an initial commercial outline and tiered pricing. Luis will append perf numbers.
[15:40] Luis Ortega: quick technical ask — Priya, can you share an anonymized traffic histogram and sample payload sizes? that'll let us size batch windows and batch latency tradeoffs.
[15:58] Priya Nair: I'll get that over, probably CSV with 1-minute granularity.
[16:12] Marco Ruiz: also send network ACLs; we have strict egress policies and need to confirm peering won't violate rules.
[16:30] Maya Chen: noted. We'll also flag one more option: a hybrid approach where initial pilot uses Hosted API with an IP allowlist to speed on-boarding, then move to Dedicated peered pools for performance guarantees. That sometimes reduces time-to-first-traffic.
[16:55] Ben Holloway: hmm hosted with allowlist — is that an easier procurement path?
[17:08] Samantha Lee: procurement tends to prefer vendor-managed initial trials if there is less upfront infra work.
[17:20] Luis Ortega: yes but hosted may complicate data residency. If shipment PII is strict, hosted is riskier; we can redact PII in transit for the hosted trial but it's an extra step.
[17:42] Priya Nair: we try to avoid PII in vendor cloud. Let's stick with peered Dedicated.
[17:58] Maya Chen: ok consensus on peered Dedicated. Next, timelines and gating: we need SOC2 + KMS guide, peering CIDRs, and your traffic sample. Once those are in we'll produce an SOW and pilot spreadsheet.
[18:22] Ben Holloway: can we get a joint customer-facing one-pager describing the co-sell motion? sales enablement wants that.
[18:36] Maya Chen: yes Hannah will draft a joint go-to-market one-pager.
[18:50] Hannah Park: I'll include close motions, reference logos, and example case studies.
[19:05] Jonas Kim: technical handoff action: we'll run a 1-hour infra deep-dive with Marco and Priya's team next week — target 7/27.
[19:24] Priya Nair: 7/27 works for us.
[19:36] Samantha Lee: procurement will need vendor contact and contract template to start legal.
[19:49] Maya Chen: I'll attach our standard partner addendum to the SOW.
[20:05] Ben Holloway: one more question — fallback policies if dedicated pool hits capacity, what's the customer-visible behavior?
[20:24] Luis Ortega: we support smart routing: short outages can be routed to hosted variants or a smaller quantized model with graceful degradation; we'll show a canary fallback policy that preserves most core responses but reduces fidelity. We log fallbacks in the Console.
[20:50] Marco Ruiz: we need to see previous incident examples — how often fallbacks triggered in similar customers.
[21:03] Luis Ortega: we'll anonymize and provide counts over the last 6 months.
[21:20] Maya Chen: ok, wrapping: agreed actions and owners in the doc. Any other quick questions?
[21:33] Ben Holloway: none from me. Thanks everyone.
[21:40] Priya Nair: no, thanks.
[21:45] Maya Chen: cool we'll send the spreadsheet and SOW draft by 7/22, security pack by 7/21, and schedule infra deep-dive on 7/27. Hannah will send the GTM one-pager. Luis and Jonas will assemble perf numbers.
[22:08] Hannah Park: noted, will follow up with calendar invites and the doc links.
[22:20] Maya Chen: perfect, talk soon.

Notes on transcript quality: occasional misattribution (SE comments sometimes labeled as "Jonas"), small ASR errors on acronyms (KV cache -> K V cash) and punctuation missing. References to docs and links included above.

End of transcript.
